newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Irish bonds ease, tracking weaker bunds.
newsitem.headline: Irish bonds ease, tracking weaker bunds.

text.p: Irish government bonds weakened in thin trade on Wednesday in line with bunds which took a beating after news of strong German M3 data and business confidence in October, dealers said.
But German dealers said they did not expect a big sell-off and that Bunds may test their highs again by end-1996.
"The market is weaker on the day. The curve has flattened up quite dramatically today, the short-end has under-performed," Riada's Padraig Garvey said.

"We had some high numbers from Germany this morning which hit bunds and the Irish market, in line with that, has traded down. In terms of spreads, we have under-performed both gilts and bunds by a couple of basis points," he added.

By 1645 GMT, the eight percent bond due 2001 eased 25 pence from Tuesday's close at 101.65 to yield 6.01 percent while the eight percent bond due 2006 slipped 37 pence from the close at 108.65 to yield 6.64 percent.
Garvey said the fact that the Irish pound remained high against the mark and held steady against sterling was positive for the market.
The Irish pound was slightly down to 2.5188 marks but was up to 1.0035 against sterling from 2.5220 marks and 1.0019 respectively at the close.
